Team lead's note, Anjali, after Tuesday's client review.
Pritam presented the logistics dashboard today. It went well. But the credits slide listed only his name, and Joseph built the entire data pipeline behind it. The two had overlapped on this project because I never split the roles clearly; that part is on me.
I watched Joseph during the presentation. He stopped taking notes after the credits slide and looked at the window for the rest of the hour. Afterwards he said to me, 'It's fine,' in a voice that wasn't fine. When I asked Pritam, he looked genuinely startled: 'I just used last month's template. I didn't think.'
Next: talk to each of them separately this week, then write clear role notes on the project sheet.

passage:
Wednesday, 10:40 p.m.
Deepak presented the pricing model to the directors today. Our pricing model. I built half the formulas and every single test case. His slides had one name at the bottom: his. I sat in the back row, clapping with everyone else, feeling like a stranger at my own project.
Afterwards I said, as lightly as I could, 'Nice job. Missed my name, though.' He actually laughed. 'Oh no, sorry yaar, total oversight, I made the deck in a rush.' Maybe it was. Our roles on this were never really clear.
But can you really 'forget' months of someone's work?
Ma called and asked why her son sounded so flat. I said I was tired. Why does it sting so much?
- Vikas

The Helsinki office was dark by four in winter. Tuan watched from the third row as Ulla presented the new booking system to the directors. Slide after slide, the search feature, the offline mode. He had spent six weeks building the offline mode.
On the last slide, "Thanks to the team," there were four names. Not his.
Afterwards, over coffee, he said as lightly as he could, "My name wasn't on the slide."
Ulla looked surprised. "Oh no. I used last quarter's template. It was just an oversight, Tuan, honestly."
Tuan nodded. "Sure." He went back to his desk and stared at his code for a long time.

qa.q: How long had Tuan spent building the offline mode?
qa.a: Six weeks.

qa.q: What was Tuan feeling as he stared at his code?
qa.a: He felt overlooked and hurt, not fully convinced by Ulla's explanation even though he said "Sure."

qa.q: What turning point is available now, before resentment grows?
qa.a: Tuan could say clearly what he'd like, such as a correction email to the directors, and Ulla could offer it without being asked.

qa.q: What might Ulla be experiencing when Tuan raises it?
qa.a: She is probably surprised and a little embarrassed, seeing the missing name as a template mistake rather than a slight.

grounding: Shows a team member left off a presentation's credits feeling overlooked, while his colleague calls it a simple oversight.

passage:
The hospital's quality committee met in the third-floor conference room. Vijay sat by the window while Reena presented the new patient-discharge checklist. He had drafted half of it. He had stayed late for two weeks testing it on Ward 4.
"This was developed by me and the nursing team," Reena said.
Vijay looked at his hands.
Afterwards, in the corridor, he said, "You didn't mention I built the Ward 4 trial."
Reena pressed her hand to her forehead. "Vijay, I'm sorry. I was nervous, and I just forgot. It wasn't on purpose."
"Okay," he said. But on the stairs down, he kept replaying "developed by me".

qa.q: Where did Vijay test the checklist?
qa.a: On Ward 4.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling as he kept replaying "developed by me"?
qa.a: He felt overlooked and hurt, as if his two weeks of work had been erased, even after Reena's apology.

qa.q: What could Vijay and Reena do now to stop this from growing?
qa.a: Agree on how shared work is credited, and ask Reena to send the committee a short note naming his part.

qa.q: How might Reena be experiencing Vijay's comment?
qa.a: She seems embarrassed and sorry, feeling it was an honest mistake made out of nerves.

grounding: Shows a team member not credited in a committee presentation feeling overlooked, while the presenter calls it an honest oversight.

Subject: Yesterday's presentation
Hi Disha,
I wanted to write this instead of letting it sit.
In yesterday's client presentation, the analytics section was introduced as your work. I built most of that model over three weeks, and my name wasn't mentioned or on the slides. I felt pretty invisible, sitting there.
I know you said afterwards it was an oversight, and I believe you didn't mean it. But our roles on this project have never been written down, and I think that's part of the problem. Could we agree who owns which parts before the next review, and could you send a short note to the client team naming both of us?
Thanks,
Chetan
